projects.name: Acme Pay signing service
projects.goal: Establish, with reproducible evidence, whether the acme-sign ECDSA P-256 verifier used by Acme Pay's signing service (release 1.4.x) accepts only well-formed signatures and meets the agreed latency budget.
constraints: Tests run on synthetic keys and messages only; no production key material enters the lab.
Sandbox runs have networking disabled and a 120 s wall-clock limit per run.
Customer CI results may be imported but are never executed here.
Nothing in this project constitutes a certification of acme-sign.

permissions.notes: Sample project. Acme Pay and all people named are fictional.

intakeQuestions.question: Which entry points of acme-sign does the signing service call in production?
intakeQuestions.answer: verify(message, signature, publicKey) and sign(message, privateKey) from the acme_sign.ecdsa module. No DER parsing path is used; signatures are raw r||s.

intakeQuestions.question: What hardware profile should latency budgets be judged against?
intakeQuestions.assumption: The lab's reference sandbox profile (4 vCPU, no SIMD restrictions). Acme's production hosts were not characterised; latency numbers are relative to this profile only.

intakeQuestions.question: Does the service ever accept signatures from external parties, or only its own?

projects.summary: Acme Pay signs payment instructions with an in-house ECDSA P-256 library, acme-sign. Baseline functional tests on release 1.4.2 found that a signature of all zeros is accepted for any message. A reviewed experiment characterised the defect, Acme shipped 1.4.3 with a range check, and retests on 1.4.3 pass. One latency question and one configuration recommendation remain open.

packData.tokenFormat: raw r||s (64 bytes) over a transaction token

items.text: Every valid signature over a valid message is accepted.
Every signature over a modified message is rejected.
Every malformed or out-of-range signature encoding is rejected.
All Wycheproof ECDSA P-256 vectors in the sample subset produce the expected result.
Verification latency p99 stays within 2.0 ms on the reference sandbox profile.
